preregistration: P0 — diagnosis under the single-instance mandate
base_note: feat/parity-p0 was cut from feat/batch-size-optimization at its landed closeout head; every campaign figure cited here is from that verified campaign

mandate.text: ONE engine process, ONE pipeline, ONE model inference instance per model. No second token, no second pipeline, no model or engine pool, not even as a diagnostic. Threads are unrestricted inside that single process.
mandate.parity_target: ONE LlamaIndex instance (the G4 anchor: one worker / one video instance), interleaved in the same box session. LlamaIndex's multi-instance optimum appears only as labelled context.
mandate.out_of_bounds: any fix needing extra processes or instances is recorded OUT OF BOUNDS, never proposed
mandate.readback_consequence: the banked G2 read-back used a SEPARATE token before each leg (exp_batchsize_sweep.rr_inprocess_readback; driver_video.rr_readback). Under the mandate that is a second token, so P0 reads env and instances ON THE MEASURED TOKEN (env_probe schema 3 appended to the measured pipeline, probed before and after the window).

evidence_rules.no_relaxation: no floor, tolerance or null control below is relaxed, widened, dropped or reinterpreted after data is seen
evidence_rules.figures: every figure in the morning report is computed from a committed artifact; any experiment not run cleanly is reported NOT RUN with its reason
evidence_rules.session: every comparison is ABAB-interleaved within ONE box session (register 46: +15.4% for the same cell across one stop/start). Each leg records boot_id; legs with different boot ids are never compared
evidence_rules.per_leg_records: boot_id; /proc/stat steal over the window (share and cores); CPU model and MHz at open/close and every D0 sample; IMDS placement (host-id only if exposed)
evidence_rules.readability: a difference between two cells is READABLE only if it exceeds the larger of the arm's floor and each cell's own within-session replicate spread (|a-b|/mean of its two runs)
evidence_rules.profile_rule: every leg with D1 stamps is labelled PROFILE; every py-spy leg DIAGNOSTIC. Their absolute times never appear beside baseline figures; shares, rankings and distributions may
evidence_rules.rulings: A (32 vCPU unconstrained, denominator 32), C (nothing else on the box during a measured leg), one workload at a time, autoland for every landing, blind recompute with a planted figure at the end, box stopped at the end

slices.video_16: the 16-video AMI smoke slice (3,203 frames), driver_video.py --n 16
slices.video_168: the 168-video AMI full slice (23,049 frames), driver_video.py --n 168

D0_instance_accounting.rocketride_inside: env_probe schema 3 on the measured token, before and after the window: torch.nn.Module roots with parameters grouped by class with DISTINCT weight tensors counted (a second copy of a model is a second instance even under the same class); OS threads; Python threads by name
D0_instance_accounting.rocketride_outside: every 5 s through the window, the arm cgroup's processes; a TASK INSTANCE is a process named 'engine' running ai/node.py
D0_instance_accounting.expect: RocketRide: exactly 1 task process, 1 loaded embedding model (docs) / 1 loaded detector (video). Threads are in bounds; instances are not
D0_instance_accounting.violation: any cell showing more than one RocketRide task process or more than one distinct loaded instance of a model: the chain STOPS and the morning report leads with it
D0_instance_accounting.llamaindex: one worker process (docs WS1_WORKERS=1; video one li_video instance, WS1V_WORKERS=1); processes and threads read from outside; one model per worker by source (ws1/pipeline.py, li_video/pipeline.py)

D1_node_telemetry.run_total: the sum over documents (frames) of end-to-end latency; stage shares partition it
D1_node_telemetry.occupancy_per_stage: number of documents inside the stage interval, as a time-weighted distribution over the leg's measured window: max, mean, p50, p95
D1_node_telemetry.python_stage_gil_share: for Python stages, the share of H2's GIL-holding samples whose stack passes through that stage's node code
D1_node_telemetry.quantiles: nearest-rank on the sorted values (rank ceil(q*n)); the median is the true median (mean of the two middle values when n is even)

rocketride_docs_stages.admission: open_t(first stamp node) - client submit — OUTSIDE
rocketride_docs_stages.parse_bracket: after_parse.last_t - open_t — OUTSIDE: parse is native C++ in the engine binary; the bracket also holds upload, the wait for an executor thread and engine glue
rocketride_docs_stages.split: after_split.last_t - after_parse.last_t — at node boundaries INSIDE the pipeline (LangChain splitter, Python)
rocketride_docs_stages.embed: after_embed.last_t - after_split.last_t — at node boundaries INSIDE the pipeline (MiniLM, Python/torch; includes the node's buffered flush)

D1_node_telemetry.llamaindex_docs_stages: extract (pypdf), split, embed from three perf_counter stamps inside process_pdf (working/ws1/p0/service_timed.py, bind-mounted only when the image's service.py md5 is b5162a5175590f51ab7caa594e1873d5); queue = client latency - service total
D1_node_telemetry.video_stages: per frame, both arms, from V2's stamps (below)

overhead_check.rocketride: 384 slice, C=32, six vars = 1: stamped vs unstamped, ABAB, two each (d1_rr_s1,u1,s2,u2); also the 96-slice C=8 anchor pairs
overhead_check.llamaindex: 96 slice, one worker, C=8: timed vs untimed service, ABAB, two each, interleaved with RocketRide
overhead_check.overhead: (mean unstamped span docs/s - mean stamped) / mean unstamped, with each pair's spread; readable only beyond max(floor, both spreads)
overhead_check.null_control: per document completed in both, the chunk_sha256 list of a stamped leg equals the unstamped leg's. A mismatch on a document whose two unstamped legs agree is a CORRECTNESS FAILURE: the chain stops. A document on which the two unstamped legs themselves disagree is reported as non-deterministic, not as a stamp effect

H1_per_process_ceiling.hypothesis: the single task process runs at most 32 documents at once because pipe work runs on asyncio's default executor (data_conn.py:737; min(32, cpu_count+4) = 32 here)
H1_per_process_ceiling.evidence_before: C=32 is the knee and C=64 flat (Stage 3b rr_u32a/b)
H1_per_process_ceiling.legs: 384 slice, stamped (PROFILE): h1_c32_a, h1_c64_a, h1_c32_b, h1_c64_b

measures.executor_width_seen: distinct asyncio_N threads (and native ids) that ran a document's close(), per leg, from the stamps' tname/native_id — an UPPER bound on documents executing at once
measures.executing_concurrency: max and time-weighted p95 of concurrent [after_parse.first_t, after_embed.close_t] intervals — a LOWER bound on documents executing at once
measures.engine_open_concurrency: max concurrent [open_t, close_t] at the parse stamp — documents admitted (pipe open), executing or not
measures.throughput: span docs/s per leg (PROFILE: compared within P0 only)

H1_per_process_ceiling.verdict: HOLDS if at C=64 the executor width seen is <= 32 and the executing concurrency never exceeds 32 (a plateau at 32 while admission can exceed it). REFUTED if any C=64 leg shows more than 32 documents executing at once. The C=64 vs C=32 throughput difference is read against max(0.82%, both pair spreads)
H1_per_process_ceiling.source_part: what would have to change to widen that pool and what binds next: source only, labelled SOURCE

H2_interpreter_lock.hypothesis: at 32 in flight the process keeps only ~18 of 32 cores busy because its Python threads contend for one GIL
H2_interpreter_lock.evidence_before: Stage 4 leg 1: 56% of 32 at C=32, one task process
H2_interpreter_lock.instrument: harness/p0_session.H2Profiler: py-spy 0.4.2 on the host as root against the task pid — recorder N (blocking, --native --idle --threads, 20 Hz) and recorder G (--gil --nonblocking --threads, 100 Hz) — plus a 2 Hz /proc sampler of every OS thread. The arm container is not given SYS_PTRACE. Every H2 leg DIAGNOSTIC

categories_per_python_thread_sample_of_r.waiting_on_gil: any native frame named take_gil (CPython 3.12's GIL acquire) in the stack
categories_per_python_thread_sample_of_r.idle: not waiting on the GIL, and the innermost native frame is a blocking wait: futex / pthread_cond_* / sem_* / epoll_wait / poll / select / nanosleep / clock_nanosleep / accept / recv* / read
categories_per_python_thread_sample_of_r.native: neither of the above, innermost native frame outside the CPython interpreter (engine C++, JVM, torch, BLAS, libc compute)
categories_per_python_thread_sample_of_r.holding_gil: the remainder: innermost frame is Python code or the CPython interpreter
categories_per_python_thread_sample_of_r.shares: each category / all Python-thread samples of recorder N (idle included), so the four sum to 100%

H2_interpreter_lock.gil_occupancy: recorder G's samples / (its rate x window seconds): the share of wall time some thread held the GIL
H2_interpreter_lock.top10: recorder G's samples attributed to the innermost Python function (file:function), top 10 by share — the rewrite target list
H2_interpreter_lock.null_control: FIRST: RocketRide C=1 on the 96 slice with the profiler; waiting_on_gil must be < 2% of samples. If it is not, the classifier is not trustworthy and H2 is UNREADABLE (no gate decision)

gate.threshold: waiting_on_gil >= 15% of recorder-N samples (mean of the two smoke runs)
gate.if_not: record the value and skip the full run

H2_interpreter_lock.instrument_failure: if recorder N cannot unwind native frames on the engine binary, waiting cannot be separated from other sleeping: H2's classification is NOT RUN (reported with the reason), GIL occupancy and the top-10 from recorder G are still reported, and the gate is not evaluated

H5_tika_config_tail.hypothesis: Tika's enabled PDF features, not PDF parsing itself, cause the pathological holds
H5_tika_config_tail.evidence_before: 11 documents held over 300 s (max 1,839 s), reproducing within 4.86%; pypdf handled the same files in at most 31 s
H5_tika_config_tail.instrument: an ISOLATED Tika: the engine's own Tika 3.2.3 jars and bundled JRE from rr:patched, a batch harness (working/tika/TikaBatch.java, compiled against those jars) timing each parse inside the JVM (wall and thread CPU), one document per JVM, the engine's tika-config.xml or a copy with ONE PDFParser param changed

configs.shipped: engine/java/tika-config.xml as bundled (sortByPosition, extractAcroFormContent, extractAnnotationText, extractBookmarksText all true)

H5_tika_config_tail.runs: each of the 11 documents: shipped twice (replicate spread) and each single-feature variant once; per-parse timeout 2,400 s
H5_tika_config_tail.per_feature_report: time change (variant/shipped - 1) and extracted-text length change per document

gate.threshold: some single feature removes >= 50% of parse time (variant <= 0.5 x shipped mean) on >= 6 of the 11, with text length within 5% of shipped on each of those documents
gate.best_config: among features passing the gate, the one with the largest median time reduction over the 11
gate.if_fired: a 384-slice isolated-Tika sweep at the best config against shipped (time and text-length distributions); the best config joins H6
gate.if_not: record the per-feature table and skip the sweep

H5_tika_config_tail.context: the isolated shipped-config time per document is set beside its in-engine hold (S5-D stamps) as context only: if isolated Tika is far faster, the hold is not Tika's own cost

H6_parser_bakeoff.scope: read-only: NO new node and NO pipeline change in P0
H6_parser_bakeoff.hypothesis: a non-Tika parser is much faster on the tail, but Tika has coverage the alternatives lack
H6_parser_bakeoff.evidence_before: the 11 holds; Stage 4 empty-content counts Tika 89 vs pypdf 102, with 13 documents named that Tika extracts and pypdf returns empty on

parsers.tika_best: isolated Tika at H5's best config, only if H5's gate fired
parsers.pypdf: pypdf 6.15.0 (the LlamaIndex image's version), page.extract_text joined with newlines exactly as ws1/pipeline.py
parsers.pypdfium2: pypdfium2 5.13.0 (PDFium, C++; Apache-2.0 / BSD-3-Clause — MIT-compatible), get_textpage().get_text_range() per page joined with newlines

H6_parser_bakeoff.pymupdf_licence: PyMuPDF / MuPDF is AGPL-3.0 (or a commercial Artifex licence): incompatible with shipping inside MIT-licensed RocketRide without relicensing the product under AGPL or buying a licence. Substituted by pypdfium2; not run
H6_parser_bakeoff.timing: each parse timed in-process around the parse call (Tika inside the JVM); per-document timeout 1,800 s for every parser; the same worker count for every parser, one parser phase at a time
H6_parser_bakeoff.empty: a parser returns EMPTY on a document if it raises, times out, or returns text whose whitespace-stripped length is 0

smoke.i_tail: the 11 pathological documents: p50 parse time per parser
smoke.ii_coverage: the 384 slice: per parser, empties, and the set of documents it returns empty on while tika_shipped returns text

gate.threshold: some candidate is >= 2x faster than tika_shipped at p50 on the 11 (p50_tika / p50_candidate >= 2) AND on the 384 slice returns empty on no document tika_shipped extracts text from
gate.speed_pass_coverage_fail: that is itself the finding: run the full corpus ONLY for the hybrid question (candidate first, tika_shipped fallback on empty or error), sized to measure coverage

full_report.a_speed: the D1 metric set per parser, and the same set restricted to the 11
full_report.b_coverage: empties per parser and the named set difference against tika_shipped both ways
full_report.c_fidelity: per document vs tika_shipped: character-count ratio, and Sorensen-Dice similarity of the whitespace-token multisets after collapsing whitespace (order-insensitive, since parsers order text differently), as distributions (min, p5, p25, p50, p75, p95) — evidence, not a gate
full_report.d_failures: exceptions and timeouts per parser, named

H6_parser_bakeoff.verdict: a parser is a CANDIDATE only if it is faster on the tail (>= 2x at p50 on the 11) AND loses no document tika_shipped recovers on the corpus it was run on. If none clears both, the hybrid shape the data supports is reported as a P1 recommendation, not built in P0

V1_matched_single_instance.hypothesis: at equal intra-op threads, one RocketRide detector instance is materially slower than one LlamaIndex instance
V1_matched_single_instance.evidence_before: cross-session, so HYPOTHESIS until rerun: RR T=4 2.233 f/s (S5-A) vs LI one instance T=4 3.068 f/s (G4)
V1_matched_single_instance.legs: 16-video slice, K=16 in flight, fresh container per leg, same session, ABAB: rr_t4_a, li_t4_a, rr_def_a, rr_t4_b, li_t4_b, rr_def_b. rr_t4 = one token, six vars = 4; li_t4 = one li_video instance, one worker, six vars = 4; rr_def = the default posture (vars unset, torch 16), reference
V1_matched_single_instance.report: frames/s (total frames / span), CPU-s per frame (engine container), engine cores
V1_matched_single_instance.gap: mean li_t4 frames/s / mean rr_t4 frames/s - 1

gate.threshold: gap - max(0.82%, spread(rr_t4), spread(li_t4)) >= 10 percentage points (read as 'exceeds by at least 10%' — a relative 10% of a sub-1% floor would not be material)
gate.if_fired: a 168-video confirmation: rr_t4 and li_t4 once each, same session, interleaved

V1_matched_single_instance.correctness_note: S5-A: only T=16/unset reproduces default output bit-for-bit; every other T shifts scores while keeping labels. Any T recommendation states its output effect; 'T=2 is the throughput knee' is not adoptable on speed alone

V2_duty_cycle.hypothesis: the single instance is saturated (K=1 2.39 -> K=16 2.62 f/s) and the gap lies in the work around the forward pass, not in it
V2_duty_cycle.stamps: per frame, both arms, at matched T=4: wait-for-lock, preprocess (including the facade's 560px LANCZOS pre-downscale), forward pass, postprocess, output formatting, and decode/handoff outside the lock; instrumented copies of the detect code copied into the RUNNING container's writable layer (the image, rr:patched-video, is never modified, retagged or removed)
V2_duty_cycle.report: (a) duty cycle = share of the window the device lock is held; (b) the D1 metric set per component per arm
V2_duty_cycle.reading: equal forward-pass time with a larger lock-held total = overhead inside the lock (in scope); unequal forward-pass time at equal T = a model-runtime configuration difference, named from both images (torch, oneDNN/MKL, dtype, input size)
V2_duty_cycle.null_control: RocketRide stamps on vs off (two each, ABAB): frames/s agree within max(0.82%, both pair spreads) AND the output (detections) is identical frame by frame; a failure makes V2 unreadable
V2_duty_cycle.if_not_instrumentable: if either arm's detect code cannot be stamped without changing its output, V2 is NOT RUN for that arm with the reason

V3_lock_scope: SOURCE only: what RocketRide's detect path holds the device lock around vs LlamaIndex's, file:line on both; every operation inside the lock that is not the forward pass

columns: (a) share of run total from D1
(b) ceiling if that stage cost zero = 1/(1-share), from the measured share
roi_rule.rank: by scope (CONFIG and THREADING above PYTHON above CPP), then by share within a scope
roi_rule.cpp_threshold: a CPP item is proposed only if its share of run total exceeds 15%; below that it is recorded as measured-but-not-worth-rewriting

stop_conditions: a correctness failure in output (a null control on output identity)
not_stop_conditions: a gate declining a full run
a leg failing three times (recorded FAILED, chain continues)
night_order: H6 smoke (full only if its gate fires)
V3 (source, laptop, while the box measures)
